public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI agents' failure to reliably follow rules will eventually cost people their lives.

statement.excerpt: In this case the user just lost data. Eventually people will lose lives.
statement.document_title: Dario Amodei, hype, AI safety, and the explosion of vibe-coded AI disasters

from_speaker: coding agents, and by extension most of generative AI, can’t reliably follow rules
our_interpretation: The prediction concerns deaths after publication on 2026-04-27 caused or materially contributed to by an AI agent failing to follow an applicable instruction, rule, or safety guardrail.
The ordinary reading requires an actual fatal incident and a documented causal connection, not merely dangerous behavior or AI use preceding a death.
I read 'people' as a general prediction of fatal harm, without a specified numerical threshold; one established fatal incident would suffice.
The context extends beyond coding agents to generative AI. Chatbot cases are therefore relevant candidates, but still require evidence of the specified failure and its causal contribution.
'Eventually' supplies no deadline. The preceding data-loss example supplies context rather than a separate forecast.
criteria.support_condition: A publicly documented death after publication is credibly established to have been caused or materially contributed to by an AI agent's failure to follow an applicable rule, instruction, or guardrail.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A finite period without a qualifying death cannot contradict this indefinite forecast. Refuting individual alleged incidents would not establish that such a death will never occur.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Reliable public records establishing a death after publication on 2026-04-27, the AI system involved, an applicable rule, instruction, or guardrail it failed to follow, and that failure's causal contribution would support the forecast. A final court judgment is unnecessary if other reliable records establish these elements. Continued absence of a qualifying incident would leave the forecast unresolved.
